text: Replace the Factorization Machine interaction scorer with an embedding-plus-MLP scorer while retaining the same seven fields, train/validation split, BCE objective, optimizer, and early-stopping rule.
rationale: The current model captures only second-order additive interactions. A nonlinear scorer could model context-dependent user-video preferences and may address the severe tab-specific ranking weaknesses. The measured request-context addition already produced a positive primary screening lift, indicating that the input fields contain incremental signal.
exact_ablation: Replace only the FM scoring function with a two-layer embedding MLP; keep the seven encoded fields, data loader, labels, BCE loss, optimizer settings, split, and checkpoint selection unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Moderate positive increase, approximately +0.003 to +0.008, if nonlinear user-video-context interactions improve within-user separation.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small-to-moderate positive increase, approximately +0.002 to +0.007, with the largest potential benefit in weak context slices; it could be flat if the MLP overfits sparse combinations.

text: Add a single low-rank cross branch to the existing embedding scorer so bounded higher-order interactions among user, video, and request-context fields are learned explicitly.
rationale: The positive request-context result suggests that context changes candidate ordering, while very low GAUC and nDCG@5 in tabs 8 and 3 suggest that additive field effects may be insufficient. A regularized cross branch is a targeted architecture change rather than a feature expansion.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one two-layer low-rank cross branch to the current FM model and sum its output with the existing logit; leave fields, loss, optimizer, and all hyperparameters other than the new branch fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small-to-moderate positive increase, approximately +0.002 to +0.006, from better context-conditioned ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Moderate positive increase, approximately +0.003 to +0.008, if cross terms correct top-five placement in weak tabs; rare combinations may instead cause volatility.

text: Replace pointwise BCE training with within-user pairwise logistic ranking loss using one positive-negative pair per eligible training user batch.
rationale: The official objective is within-user ordering, whereas the current model is trained pointwise. The gap between useful global ordering and weak top-five slices makes an ordering-aligned objective a high-information alternative, though sparse users may provide few valid pairs.
exact_ablation: Replace only BCE with pairwise logistic loss over sampled same-user positive-negative pairs; preserve the FM architecture, seven fields, optimizer, split, pair construction cutoff, and evaluation code.

expected_effect.GAUC: Moderate positive increase, approximately +0.003 to +0.009, because optimization directly rewards positive-over-negative ordering within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.005; pair sampling may improve broad ordering without reliably improving the first five positions.

text: Use a top-rank-weighted pairwise loss that emphasizes the highest-scoring positive-negative violations during training.
rationale: nDCG@5 is materially lower than GAUC in the current result, and the weakest tabs show that top-five quality is the principal user-facing weakness. A top-weighted ranking loss directly targets this metric tradeoff rather than adding more fields.
exact_ablation: Replace only the current BCE objective with a top-rank-weighted pairwise logistic loss using model-score-based violation weights; retain the FM, features, optimizer, batch construction, and split.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive or slightly negative change, approximately -0.002 to +0.004, because emphasizing top violations can sacrifice some broad pair ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Moderate positive increase, approximately +0.003 to +0.010, if the loss concentrates learning on candidates that can enter the top five.

text: Increase the FM interaction embedding dimension from 16 to 32 without changing the fields or training procedure.
rationale: The current seven-field model may be capacity-limited when representing user-video-context interactions. This is a clean low-risk capacity ablation, especially because the request-context screen showed measurable incremental signal but the observed gain was modest.
exact_ablation: Change only interaction_dimension from 16 to 32; keep the seven fields, FM equations, BCE objective, learning rate, L2, batch size, seed, split, and stopping rule fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, if additional dimensions capture stable context interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.003; extra capacity may not improve top-five ordering in sparse slices.

text: Reduce FM interaction embedding dimension from 16 to 8 to regularize sparse context combinations.
rationale: Request-context gains vary substantially by date, and several small context segments are unstable. Lower capacity could reduce memorization of rare tab-hour combinations and improve temporal robustness, although it may underfit warm users.
exact_ablation: Change only interaction_dimension from 16 to 8; keep fields, FM equations, loss, optimizer, L2, seed, split, and checkpoint selection unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Flat to slightly positive, approximately -0.002 to +0.003, if regularization improves stability across context slices.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Flat to slightly negative, approximately -0.003 to +0.002, because lower capacity may lose useful personalized top-five distinctions.

text: Represent hour as a cyclic pair of normalized sine and cosine values instead of a categorical hour field.
rationale: Hour segments 3 and 4 have particularly weak ranking metrics, suggesting that independent categorical hour embeddings may generalize poorly across adjacent times. A cyclic representation shares strength between neighboring hours while preserving impression-time availability.
exact_ablation: Replace only the categorical hour field with two cyclic numeric features sin(2πhour/24) and cos(2πhour/24); retain tab, weekday, the other five fields, FM implementation, and training configuration.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, from smoother temporal generalization within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, if adjacent-hour behavior is similar; categorical effects may otherwise be stronger.

text: Remove weekday while retaining hour, tab, and the original five fields to test whether the measured request-context benefit is driven by weekday rather than the more granular context fields.
rationale: The completed experiment added three context fields together, so their individual contributions are unidentified. This single-field ablation is a useful portfolio member because it can isolate unnecessary capacity and distinguish robust hour/tab signal from weaker calendar effects.
exact_ablation: Remove only the weekday categorical field; retain tab, hour, user_id, video_id, author_id, duration bucket, model, loss, optimizer, and split unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small negative or flat change, approximately -0.003 to +0.001, if weekday contributes little incremental within-user ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small negative or flat change, approximately -0.003 to +0.001, with no expected benefit unless weekday overfits.

text: Add impression date as a categorical field to model short-term temporal drift beyond weekday and hour.
rationale: The request-context screen had positive lift on three of four dates, with especially large late holdout-day gains, indicating possible non-periodic temporal variation. Date is known at impression time, but the small number of dates creates a clear overfitting risk.
exact_ablation: Add only a train-vocabulary categorical date field; retain all existing fields, FM architecture, BCE objective, optimizer, and split policy unchanged, with unknown date handling for later dates.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.004, if date captures temporal drift that reorders candidates within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or negative change, approximately -0.003 to +0.004, because date memorization may improve some periods while harming generalization.

text: Apply feature dropout only to the request-context fields during FM training so the model does not rely excessively on unstable tab-hour combinations.
rationale: The context addition is promising but its daily primary lift has high variability, and several context slices are weak. Context-specific dropout could preserve the signal while improving robustness to distribution shift and rare combinations.
exact_ablation: During training only, independently mask tab, hour, and weekday categorical inputs with probability 0.10; leave inference inputs, fields, FM equations, loss, optimizer, and all other settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, if robustness improves across unstable context slices.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.002 to +0.004; masking may reduce precise top-five personalization.

text: Lower the learning rate from 0.001 to 0.0005 while retaining the same model, fields, loss, batch size, and early-stopping patience.
rationale: The observed request-context gain is close to the scale of daily variability, so optimization noise may materially affect the checkpoint. A smaller step size may stabilize the interaction embeddings and improve reproducibility, especially in weak context slices.
exact_ablation: Change only learning_rate from 0.001 to 0.0005; preserve architecture, fields, BCE, batch size, seed, maximum epochs, patience, split, and checkpoint selection.

expected_effect.GAUC: Flat to slightly positive, approximately -0.002 to +0.003, through more stable embedding optimization.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Flat to slightly positive, approximately -0.003 to +0.003; slower optimization may miss the best checkpoint under the fixed epoch budget.

text: Replace uniform BCE minibatches with user-stratified minibatches that preserve multiple impressions per user while keeping the natural validation distribution unchanged.
rationale: The official metrics are within-user ranking metrics, and sparse-positive users show very different top-five behavior from users with more positives. More user-coherent training batches may expose the model to within-user contrasts instead of letting high-volume users dominate optimization.
exact_ablation: Change only training minibatch construction to sample a fixed number of users and impressions per user per batch, without changing row inclusion, labels, model, loss, optimizer, or validation scoring.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.005, if user-level contrast structure is learned more evenly.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or negative change, approximately -0.002 to +0.004, because rebalancing training users can alter emphasis away from the natural impression distribution.
